title: indigo_libs: azimuth due north is published as 360 instead of 0
description:
Owner decision (2026-11-19): an azimuth of 360 is a defect, due north has to be 0. Found by the version comparison of ticket 9fe7f46e-cf10-4f1e-8b3a-cca9aa1f16f1.

Observation (mount_synscan on its simulator, home position at the north celestial pole, northern site): MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES.AZ published through the library is 360.000000000 (2 pi minus about 1e-15 rad) at connect, after a site change and, once the driver's poll uses indigo_update_coordinates(), on every poll. Cause: indigo_cartesian_to_spherical() in indigo_libs/indigo_align.c maps a tiny negative angle to just below 2 pi (spoint.a = -atan2(y, x); if (spoint.a < 0) spoint.a += TWO_PI), and indigo_radec_to_altaz() passes it on in degrees; nothing brings a value that rounds to a full circle back to 0. Callers: indigo_mount_driver.c (connect and indigo_update_coordinates()), so every mount driver on the library path is affected, plus any other user of these functions.

Fix: the azimuth returned for the horizontal coordinates must be in [0, 360) also after rounding to the precision at which it is published, so that due north is 0 and never 360; decide the narrowest correct place (indigo_radec_to_altaz() or the spherical conversion) after checking every caller of the changed function, and report the choice and the callers. No change for azimuths that are not within rounding of a full circle.

Tests: unit test of the conversion at and around due north (pole from both sides of the meridian, tiny positive and negative hour angles, southern site where the pole is at azimuth 180) and a mount_simulator case that the published azimuth at the pole is 0; run the affected unit and mount_simulator tests.
